title: Game HUD state and zone map
summary: Inventory every game-interface state and place status, objectives and controls in stable zones so an agent can rebuild the HUD in the user stack instead of copying a sample scene.
when_to_use: The user is designing a playable game overlay, pause flow, or touch controls.
avoid_when: The surface is a marketing page or an admin dashboard.

anatomy.purpose: Lists gameplay, pause, settings, fail, win, loading and touch-control states before any visual styling.
Orders survival and status above objectives, then immediate feedback, then flavor.
Reserves corners and edges for status, objectives and touch controls, leaving the play path clear.
Connects visible meters to game state instead of reimplementing rules inside the view.

tokens.name: hud.zone.inset
tokens.purpose: Padding that keeps controls inside the device safe area.

tokens.name: hud.numeric.width
tokens.purpose: Fixed width for values that change digits during play.

tokens.name: hud.alert.danger
tokens.purpose: One color role for danger, distinct from reward and objective.

states.name: gameplay
states.behavior: Shows only the status and controls needed while playing.

states.name: pause
states.behavior: Pauses interaction and puts resume first.

states.name: fail
states.behavior: Offers a retry without covering the cause of failure.

responsive: Check the longest expected numbers and labels at phone width and at desktop width.
Add touch controls only when mobile play is actually in scope.
accessibility: Keep touch targets large enough to hit while the device is moving.
Do not convey danger by color alone.
implementation_steps: List the states the user actually needs.
Assign each readout to a zone and a token role.
Implement the layout in the user stack, bound to existing game state.
Verify text fit, overlap and focus states with the longest values.
